prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architecture and active sites.

statement.case_for: Zeolite and molecular-sieve design is a clear case of architecture determining function. Structure-directing agents, new framework topologies and engineered acid and metal sites let chemists place catalytic sites inside pores of defined size, and this is the basis of fluid catalytic cracking, hydrocracking, methanol-to-hydrocarbons, selective catalytic reduction of NOx and many fine-chemical processes. The structural evidence is exceptionally strong, because frameworks have been solved and refined for decades, and the impact is industrial, lasting and independently confirmed. Zones's template chemistry and Davis's framework work deliver the synthetic control, and Corma's work links framework and active-site design to catalytic function. Chemistry has recognised catalysis and materials architecture many times, but not this area.
statement.case_against: Not one colleague ranked B018 in the opening round, so my first place stands alone and I cannot treat it as a committee view. The field is also old and diffuse. Barrer, Milton, Breck and others laid the foundations and are outside the credited list, Yu and Tsapatsis made major contributions that a three-name limit excludes, and the subject can be read as incremental industrial refinement rather than a single discovery. Because zeolites are my own research field, I may overrate its visibility to a wider committee, and a prize for it may be hard to justify next to the chemical-biology candidates that most colleagues favour.

responses.point: Linke ranks base editing (B060) first as a conceptually clean chemical principle with extensive independent confirmation and clinical trials under way, with the Liu-lab trio Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as the most coherent configuration.
responses.response: I agree that the principle is original and well confirmed, and I ranked it fourth for that reason. I disagree on the trio. Komor and Gaudelli were lead authors of the founding studies, but the intellectual design came from Liu, and Kondo and Nishida independently reported a deaminase-based approach (Target-AID). A trio drawn only from one laboratory therefore overstates the record. If B060 goes forward I would credit Liu alone or reopen the question of Kondo and Nishida. I also hold that the 2020 CRISPR prize recognised the nuclease and that the chemistry here lies in the deaminase engineering, so that point should be argued explicitly in the citation.

responses.point: Aili puts targeted protein degradation (B012) first, naming Crews, Deshaies and Handa, because induced proximity is a general design principle that opens undruggable targets, and she notes that the Ciulli and Gray contributions complicate attribution.
responses.response: The concept is strong, but I question the claim that the credit can be settled on the present evidence. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which is a separate mechanistic discovery that explains molecular glues, whereas Crews and Deshaies conceived PROTACs. Those two strands may not fit one citation. Ciulli's VHL ligands and the ternary-complex structures are the part I weigh most, because they show by structure how the induced proximity works. Without an approved degrader I also see the clinical payoff as unproven, so I would rank B012 above its present placement only if the committee can settle the PROTAC versus molecular-glue split.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks nitrogenase structure and mechanism (B051) second, valuing structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo-cofactor with the central light atom as visible mechanism.
responses.response: I share the respect for these structures, and I ranked B051 seventh. Rees and Einsle's structural work, including the interstitial carbide, is very convincing as evidence. My reservation, which you also state, is that the structure is settled but the N2 reduction mechanism and the substrate-binding site are not, so a citation would have to stay on structure and cofactor identity. That is narrower than the claim of a mechanistic breakthrough, and Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe would be left out of a three-name prize, so I would not put it ahead of the candidates with clearer attribution.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B055) first, with Buchwald and Hartwig, as a simple, general bond-forming method with more than 25 years of confirmation, and treats Kosugi as a precursor.
responses.response: I agree with the two-person attribution and with treating Kosugi's tin-amide coupling as a precursor rather than the general method. My difference is on distinctiveness. I see the C-N reaction as a major methodology that extends the cross-coupling logic recognised in 2010, whereas zeolite design opens a separate architecture-to-function area that the Prize has not covered. I would nevertheless accept B055 as a sound, clean option if the committee wants a well-attributed synthetic-methods prize, and I note Hartwig also appears in the C-H functionalisation candidate, so he can be recognised only once.

uncertainties: Whether any colleague will support B018 given that no one ranked it in the opening round, and whether the three-name set Corma, Davis, Zones is the right one or should include Yu or Tsapatsis.
Whether early zeolite pioneers outside the credited list (for example Barrer, Milton, Breck) create an attribution problem that the supplied credited names cannot resolve.
Whether base editing (B060) should be credited to Liu alone or with Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands of B012 can be combined into one citation, and what the clinical record will show once degraders are approved.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional conflict is apparent from my profile for the candidates on the shortlist. B018 lies in my own research field (zeolites and porous framework materials) and I know that community professionally, including credited names such as Jihong Yu, but my profile records no collaboration, mentorship or institutional tie to Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu or Tsapatsis. I flag the field proximity for transparency and would step back if a closer tie were shown.
